## Create the folders

```{r create folders, eval=FALSE}

dir.create("output")
dir.create("figures")
dir.create("reports")

```

## Load necessary libraries

```{r libraries, include = FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(here)            # To manage project file paths reproducibly
library(dplyr)           # For data manipulation and wrangling
library(VIM)             # For KNN imputation and visualization of missing data
library(gtsummary)       # To create publication-ready summary and regression tables
library(flextable)       # To export  gtsummary tables in a Word Doc, ideal for gtsummary

library(survival)        # For survival analysis (Kaplan–Meier and Cox proportional hazards models)

library(flextable)       # To save tables not created by gtsummary()

library(emmeans)         # To estimate contrasts from models containing interactions.
```

## 1 Import data and define variables

```{r import, include = TRUE}

Outcome <- read.csv(
  here("data", "Outcome_data.csv"),
  header = TRUE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

Outcome <- Outcome %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(PID, QCODE), as.character),
    
    across(c(AGS, YEARS,BLDLOSS, BMI, CATHPERIOD, FUPM, HOSPTIME,OPRTIME,
             POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI_T), as.numeric),
    
    across(c(REC011, ANASTOMO,BLDCOMPLEAK,BLDCOMPRETN,BLDCOMPVOID,BLDSPASM,CATH,CENTER,
             CLAVIENCLASS,EPIDURAL,GENDER, GU30, GU90N, GUER30, GUER90, HEMAT, 
             HISTOINJ,ILEUS, INCCOMPBLEED, INCCOMPINF, INCCOMPSCAR, NARC, 
             NONARC, PAIN, PREOPEPISODE1, PREOPRNPLN, PREOPRNSCR, PREOPTYPEU1,
             PREOPVURGRADE, PROC365, STENT, SURGIND, SURGTECH2, TRT2, UDR7M,
             URCOMPCVUR, URCOMPINJ, URCOMPOBST, URCOMPSTEN, POSTUTI, VURPHASE,
             VURSIDE, RECGRADE_MAX), as.factor)
  )

str(Outcome) # 412 obs. of 55 variables

```

## 2 Data Imputation using KNN (k-nearest neighbors)

```{r imputation, include = TRUE}

# Missingness in the dataset
m_outcome <- colSums(is.na(Outcome)) / nrow(Outcome) * 100
print(m_outcome)


# KNN imputation
Outcome_knn <- Outcome # create a temporary dataset copy for KNN using scaled variables

# Convert categorical variables
cat_vars <- c(
  "GENDER","PREOPVURGRADE", "VURPHASE","VURSIDE",
  "UDR7M","PREOPRNSCR","HISTOINJ","SURGIND",
  "CENTER","TRT2", "SURGTECH2",
  "PREOPEPISODE1", "PREOPRNPLN","PREOPTYPEU1"
)
Outcome_knn[cat_vars] <- lapply(Outcome_knn[cat_vars], as.factor)

# Scale continuous variables
continuous_vars <- c("AGS", "BMI", "YEARS")
Outcome_knn[continuous_vars] <- scale(Outcome_knn[continuous_vars])


# KNN imputation without subsetting the dataset
Outcome_knn <- kNN(
  Outcome_knn,
  variable = c("PREOPEPISODE1", "PREOPRNPLN", "PREOPTYPEU1"),  # Variables to impute
  dist_var = c("AGS","GENDER","BMI", # Variables used to compute patient similarity
    "PREOPVURGRADE","VURPHASE","VURSIDE","UDR7M",
    "PREOPRNSCR","HISTOINJ","SURGIND","YEARS",
    "TRT2"
  ),
  k = 5,
  imp_var = FALSE
)


# CENTER + TRT2 + SURGTECH2 together may overweight institutional structure, which means clustering patients by institution rather than biology → keep only one of them, I will keep "TRT2".

Out <- Outcome   # New dataset for analysis including imputed variables 

Out$PREOPEPISODE1 <- Outcome_knn$PREOPEPISODE1
Out$PREOPRNPLN   <- Outcome_knn$PREOPRNPLN
Out$PREOPTYPEU1  <- Outcome_knn$PREOPTYPEU1
```

## 3 Recode and create (composite) variables

```{r recode}

# Recode SURGIND into SURGIND2

Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(
    SURGIND2 = case_when(
      SURGIND == 4 ~ 1,
      SURGIND == 3 ~ 2,
      SURGIND == 1 ~ 3,
      SURGIND == 2 ~ 4,
      SURGIND %in% c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) ~ 5,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    SURGIND2 = factor(SURGIND2)
  )


# Create a new variable LUTD by combining BLDCOMPRETN, BLDCOMPVOID, BLDCOMPLEAK
Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(
    LUTD = case_when(
      BLDCOMPRETN == 1 |
      BLDCOMPVOID == 1 |
      BLDCOMPLEAK == 1 ~ 1,

      BLDCOMPRETN == 0 &
      BLDCOMPVOID == 0 &
      BLDCOMPLEAK == 0 ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    LUTD = factor(LUTD)
  )


# Create a new variable OBST by combining URCOMPOBST, URCOMPSTEN, ANASTOMO
Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(
    OBST = case_when(
      URCOMPOBST == 1 |
      URCOMPSTEN == 1 |
      ANASTOMO == 1 ~ 1,

      URCOMPOBST == 0 &
      URCOMPSTEN == 0 &
      ANASTOMO == 0 ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    OBST = factor(OBST)
  )


# Create a new variable SURG by combining INCCOMPBLEED, INCCOMPINF, INCCOMPSCAR
Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(
    SURG = case_when(
      INCCOMPBLEED == 1 |
      INCCOMPINF == 1 |
      INCCOMPSCAR == 1 ~ 1,

      INCCOMPBLEED == 0 &
      INCCOMPINF == 0 &
      INCCOMPSCAR == 0 ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    SURG = factor(SURG)
  )

# Create a new variable GU90 by combining no readmission (0) and planned readmission (2)
Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(
    GU90 = recode(as.character(GU90N),
                  "0" = "0",
                  "1" = "1",
                  "2" = "0"),
    GU90 = factor(GU90)
  )


# Create a categorical variable CATHPERIOD_G for the numerical variable CATHPERIOD
Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(CATHPERIOD_G = case_when(
    CATHPERIOD <= 3 ~ "Early removal ≤3 days",
    CATHPERIOD > 3 & CATHPERIOD <= 7 ~ "Standard removal 4–7 days",
    CATHPERIOD > 7 ~ "Delayed removal >7 days",
  ))

Out$CATHPERIOD_G <- factor(
  Out$CATHPERIOD_G, 
  levels = c("Early removal ≤3 days", "Standard removal 4–7 days", "Delayed removal >7 days")
)


# For the sensitivity analysis for missing outcome data using two extreme assumptions: Best-case scenario: all missing recurrence outcomes are assumed to be no recurrence (0). | Worst-case scenario: all missing recurrence outcomes are assumed to be recurrence (1).

Out$REC011 <- as.numeric(as.character(Out$REC011))

Out$REC011_best <- ifelse(
  is.na(Out$REC011),
  0,
  Out$REC011
)

Out$REC011_worst <- ifelse(
  is.na(Out$REC011),
  1,
  Out$REC011
)


# Recode complications

comp_vars <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS"
)

Out[comp_vars] <- lapply(
  Out[comp_vars],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

Out$ANY <- as.numeric(
  rowSums(
    Out[, comp_vars],
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) > 0
)

minor_vars <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS"
)

Out$MINOR <- as.numeric(
  rowSums(
    Out[, minor_vars],
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) > 0
)


major_vars <- c(
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ"
)

Out$MAJOR <- as.numeric(
  rowSums(
    Out[, major_vars],
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) > 0
)


# Convert variables to appropriate data types for analysis
Out <- Out %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(PID, QCODE), as.character),
    
    across(c(AGS, YEARS,BLDLOSS, BMI, CATHPERIOD, FUPM, HOSPTIME,OPRTIME,
             POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI_T), as.numeric),
    
    across(c(REC011, REC011_best, REC011_worst, ANASTOMO,BLDCOMPLEAK,BLDCOMPRETN,
             BLDCOMPVOID,BLDSPASM,CATH,CENTER,CLAVIENCLASS,EPIDURAL,GENDER,
             GU30, GU90N, GUER30, GUER90, HEMAT, 
             HISTOINJ,ILEUS, INCCOMPBLEED, INCCOMPINF, INCCOMPSCAR, NARC, 
             NONARC, PAIN, PREOPEPISODE1, PREOPRNPLN, PREOPRNSCR, PREOPTYPEU1,
             PREOPVURGRADE, PROC365, STENT, SURGIND, SURGTECH2, TRT2, UDR7M,
             URCOMPCVUR, URCOMPINJ, URCOMPOBST, URCOMPSTEN, POSTUTI, VURPHASE,
             VURSIDE, RECGRADE_MAX, SURGIND2, LUTD, OBST, SURG, GU90,
             CATHPERIOD_G, ANY, MINOR, MAJOR), as.factor)
  )

str(Out) # 412 obs. of 66 variables



```


## 4 Descriptive analysis: BEFORE weighting and matching

```{r descriptive, warning=FALSE}

# Baseline characteristics
table1<- Out %>%
  mutate(YEARS = factor(YEARS)) %>%   # Convert only within this pipeline  
  dplyr::select(YEARS, AGS, GENDER, BMI, HISTOINJ, SURGIND2, PREOPVURGRADE, VURSIDE, UDR7M, 
         VURPHASE, PREOPTYPEU1, PREOPEPISODE1, PREOPRNPLN, PREOPRNSCR,
         SURGTECH2, CENTER, TRT2
  ) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = TRT2,  # for stratification
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}-{p75})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)" 
    ),
    digits = all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1),  # n = 0 decimals, p = 1 decimal
    missing = "ifany",  # shows missing only when present
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  add_p(
    test = list(
      YEARS ~ "chisq.test"
    ),  
  pvalue_fun = ~style_pvalue(.x, digits = 3)) %>%  #  3 decimals 
  bold_labels()

table1

table1 %>%
  as_flex_table() %>%
  flextable::save_as_docx(path = "output/baseline.docx")

## Treatment distribution change over time using a chi-square test

tab_year <- table(Out$YEARS, Out$Treatment)

chisq.test(tab_year)

p_value_year <- chisq.test(tab_year)$p.value

p_label <- ifelse(
  p_value_year < 0.001,
  "Chi-square p < 0.001",
  paste0(
    "Chi-square p = ",
    format.pval(p_value_year, digits = 3)
  )
)

p_label 

# Proportion plot for treatment across 

plot_data1 <- Out %>%
  count(YEARS, Treatment) %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

pt <- ggplot(

######## Postoperative UTI outcome as time-to-event outcome

# Create labeled TRT2 variable only for survival analysis
Out$Treatment <- factor(
  Out$TRT2,
  levels = c(0,1),
  labels = c("Cohen", "Lich–Gregoir")
)

surv_object <- Surv(time = Out$POSTUTIFUP, event = Out$POSTUTI== 1)
fit <- survfit(surv_object ~ Treatment , data = Out)

p_u <- ggsurvplot(
  fit,
  data = Out,
  fun="event",  # Show cumulative incidence (1 - survival)
  pval = FALSE,
  pval.size = 4,
  pval.coord = c(0, 0.9),  #  c(x,y) according to my x and y scale
  conf.int = TRUE,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.y.text = FALSE,   # to remove text from y-axis in the risk table
  # risk.table.title = "At risk",
  risk.table.fontsize = 4,   # ontrols numbers in table
  xlim = c(0, 135),
  break.time.by = 12,
  xlab = "Follow-up time",
  ylab = "Cumulative incidence of postopetative symptomatic UTI",
  palette = c("#482878", "#2E8B8B"),    # instead of "#ADD8E6", "#00008B"
  legend.title = "Treatment",
  legend.labs = c("Cohen Group", "Lich-Gregoir Group"),
  ylim = c(0, 1) # Force y-axis from 0 to 1
)

# calculate P-value from ggsurvplot (pval = TRUE), then turn it off

p_u$plot <- p_u$plot +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 20,
    y = 0.90,
    label = "Log rank test p = 0.058",
    size = 4
  )

#-----------------------
# Customize the plot
#-----------------------
p_u$plot <- p_u$plot +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 135),
    breaks = seq(0, 135, 12)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 100, 1), "%"),
```

## 6 Do weighting: using ATO (Recommended)

```{r weightingATO}

# In R formula syntax, use *, not just : if you want both main effects and interaction.
# Ex: PREOPVURGRADE + VURPHASE + PREOPVURGRADE:VURPHASE = PREOPVURGRADE * VURPHASE

set.seed(123)

w.out <- weightit(
  TRT2 ~ AGS + YEARS + GENDER + BMI + PREOPRNPLN + HISTOINJ +
    SURGIND2 + PREOPVURGRADE + VURSIDE + UDR7M + VURPHASE +
    PREOPEPISODE1 + PREOPTYPEU1 + PREOPRNSCR + SURGTECH2,
  data = Out,
  method = "ps",
  estimand = "ATO",   # ATE = Average Treatment Effect = this is standard inverse probability of treatment weighting
  stabilize = FALSE   # To weight based on stabilized IPTW to reduce variability in weights (reduce extreme weights)
)
Out$weights <- w.out$weights  # Add weights to the dataset
write.csv(Out, "data/weighted_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

summary(w.out$weights)


# Table for balance
# This gives: SMD before and after weighting, and flagged imbalance (>0.1)
bal <- cobalt::bal.tab(w.out, un = TRUE, ESS = TRUE, m.threshold = 0.1)  # ESS to calculate ESS separately by treatment group
# un=TRUE shows imbalance before AND after weighting, un=FALSE shows only after weighting
bal 

bal_df <- as.data.frame(bal$Balance)
smd_table <- bal_df %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = rownames(bal_df),
    SMD_Before = round(abs(Diff.Un), 3),   
    SMD_After  = round(abs(Diff.Adj), 3)
  ) %>% # you are taking the absolute value of the standardized mean differences before and after weighting
  dplyr::select(Variable, SMD_Before, SMD_After) # SMDs for each covariate individually, before and after weighting

smd_table %>%
  flextable() %>%
  save_as_docx(path = "output/SMD_w.docx")


# Figure for balance - Love plot
# Review guidelines to decide on plotting Standardized or Absolute Mean Differences
pl <- love.plot(
  w.out,
  threshold = 0.1,
  abs = TRUE, # As SMD sign is meaningless for balance, show only absolute SMDs using abs = TRUE (the correct interpretation of SMD): Because SMD direction (+/-) is meaningless, only magnitude matters
  stats = "mean.diffs",       # forces SMD instead of raw differences
  var.order = "unadjusted",   # Orders variables based on imbalance before matching
  drop.distance = TRUE,      # To exclude the distance from the plot
  sample.names = c("Before overlap weighting", "After overlap weighting"),
  size = 4,
    var.names = c(
    AGS = "Age at surgery",
    YEARS = "Year of surgery",
    BMI = "Body mass index",
    GENDER = "Female gender",
    PREOPRNPLN = "Preop pyelonephritis",
    HISTOINJ = "History of injection",
    VURSIDE = "Right-sided VUR",
    UDR7M = "Ureteral dilation ≥ 7mm",
    PREOPTYPEU1 = "Preop febrile UTIs",
    PREOPRNSCR = "Preop renal scarring",
    VURPHASE_1 = "Reflux: voiding phase",
    VURPHASE_2 = "Reflux: filling phase",
    VURPHASE_3 = "Reflux: filling + voiding",
    SURGTECH2_1 = "Surgeon experience ≥100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_2 = "Surgeon experience 50-100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_3 = "Surgeon experience <50 operations",
    PREOPEPISODE1_1 = "Preop UTI episodes: 1",
    PREOPEPISODE1_2 = "Preop UTI episodes: 2",
    PREOPEPISODE1_3 = "Preop UTI episodes: ≥3",
    SURGIND2_1 = "Indication: breakthrough UTI",
    SURGIND2_2 = "Indication: high-grade reflux (III-V)",
    SURGIND2_3 = "Indication: poor compliance to medical treatment",
    SURGIND2_4 = "Indication: ineffective/poorly tolerated CAP",
    SURGIND2_5 = "Indication: other",
    PREOPVURGRADE_3 = "Preop VUR grade: III",
    PREOPVURGRADE_4 = "Preop VUR grade: IV",
    PREOPVURGRADE_5 = "Preop VUR grade: V"
  )
  )

pl <- pl +
    scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Before overlap weighting" = "#0072B2",
      "After overlap weighting" = "#D55E00"
    )
  ) +
    labs(
      x = "Absolute Standardized Differences",
      subtitle = "Overlap population of all children"
  ) +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      panel.background = element_blank(), 
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.3, "cm"),
      panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
   )

ggsave ("figures/love_plot_w.png", plot = pl, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)

# Compute mean SMD
smd_df <- bal$Balance
mean_smd_before <- mean(abs(smd_df$Diff.Un), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before matching
mean_smd_after <- mean(abs(smd_df$Diff.Adj), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before matching
mean_smd <- data.frame(
  Mean_SMD_Before = mean_smd_before,

)

mean_smd

```
 
- CENTER will not included in the propensity score because there is one center that did not contribute cases in one treatment technique + two other centers did not show a great overlap: a good overlap is only exist in one center.

- What does the ESS of 239 mean clinically?
It does not mean that only 239 children were analyzed.
You still include all 412 children, but their contributions differ:
A child with a high overlap weight contributes more information.
A child with a near-zero overlap weight contributes very little.
The analysis is effectively equivalent to having a randomized comparison in approximately 239 patients.

- Why did you lose about 42% of effective information?
Because your original cohort likely contains patients where treatment choice was almost predetermined.
For example:
very severe VUR → almost always treated with one technique
certain surgeon experience levels → almost always associated with one technique
certain patient characteristics → strongly favor one technique
Those patients cannot provide much information about comparative effectiveness, because there is little realistic alternative treatment.
ATO appropriately reduces their influence.

- One thing I would definitely report
Because ATO changes the target population, describe it explicitly:
Instead of:
"We evaluated all 412 children..."
write something like:
"The original cohort included 412 children. Treatment effects were estimated using overlap weighting, which emphasizes patients with comparable probabilities of receiving either surgical technique. The resulting effective sample size was 239 patients."

- Your results suggest good overlap
The combination of:
✅ Perfect balance
✅ No extreme weights
✅ Equal weighted treatment groups
✅ ESS ≈239
suggests that your data contain a meaningful overlap population.
This is actually a very favorable situation for ATO.

- Because conventional inverse probability of treatment weighting resulted in residual covariate imbalance and extreme weights, overlap weighting was used as the primary approach. Overlap weighting estimates the average treatment effect among patients with clinical equipoise, where either treatment technique could plausibly have been selected.

- Comparing matching and weighting:
Because ATO avoids discarding patients, it often provides:
narrower confidence intervals
better statistical power
provided the propensity model is appropriate.

- ATO did not reduce your analysis to a tiny selected subgroup. It focused the causal comparison on the substantial proportion of children for whom both surgical techniques were clinically plausible.

- The core issue of estimand choice: does ATO answer the clinical question you actually want to answer, or are you using it only because it gives better balance?
In my case: I can apply ATO, and my clinical question can actually provide a strong justification for it — but I need to frame the research question appropriately. I should not present ATO as merely a technical solution to improve SMDs.

What is your clinical question?
You are not asking: "What is the effect of Technique A versus Technique B in all children with unilateral VUR?"
You are asking something closer to: "Among children with unilateral VUR who are candidates for either surgical technique, is one technique associated with better outcomes?"

Therefore, the clinically relevant question becomes:
"When surgeons have a genuine choice between techniques, which one performs better?"
That is exactly what ATO estimates.

The key is that you must define this before analysis.
Do not write: "We used overlap weighting because IPTW failed."
That makes it look like a data-driven rescue method.
Instead write something like:"Because the objective was to compare surgical techniques among children for whom either approach could reasonably be selected, the target estimand was the average treatment effect in the overlap population (ATO). Overlap weighting was selected a priori to estimate this effect."
This is a much stronger justification.

How I would frame your objective
Instead of: "To compare outcomes between two surgical techniques for unilateral VUR."
I would write: "To compare postoperative outcomes between two surgical techniques among children with unilateral VUR who were eligible for either approach."
This aligns naturally with ATO.


## 7 Descriptive analysis: AFTER weighting

```{r descriptivew, warning=FALSE}

# Out is the dataset with added weights
# Simply having a weights column in your dataset is not sufficient for tbl_svysummary(). The survey design object is how the survey package knows which variable contains the analysis weights and how to use them correctly.

# Create survey design object using overlap weights
design_ato <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1,   #  ids = CENTER means that patients are clustered within centers, use ids = ~1 if there is no clustering
# however, the survey package's cluster-robust variance estimation is not very reliable with very few clusters. Many statistical texts recommend caution when the number of clusters is small (often <20–30).
  data = Out,
  weights = ~weights
)

# Weighted baseline characteristics
table1w <- design_ato %>%
  tbl_svysummary(
    by = TRT2,    # for stratification
    include = c(
      YEARS, AGS, GENDER, BMI, HISTOINJ, SURGIND2, PREOPVURGRADE, VURSIDE, UDR7M, 
         VURPHASE, PREOPTYPEU1, PREOPEPISODE1, PREOPRNPLN, PREOPRNSCR,
         SURGTECH2, CENTER    # generally we should not include TRT2 in include list
  ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}-{p75})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1),
    missing = "ifany",  # shows missing only when present
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  # add_p(pvalue_fun = ~style_pvalue(.x, digits = 3)) %>% # add_p() is not informative after weighting
  bold_labels()

table1w

table1w %>%
  as_flex_table() %>%
  flextable::save_as_docx(
    path = "output/baseline_w.docx"
  )

```

Pearson's χ² test with Rao–Scott adjustment is a version of the usual chi-square test that is modified for weighted survey data (or other analyses involving complex weighting). In your case, it appears because you are using tbl_svysummary() with an object created using svydesign() and your ATO weights.

Although follow-up duration differed between groups, it was not included as a covariate because it is a post-treatment variable and may introduce bias if adjusted for. Outcomes defined within fixed follow-up windows were analyzed according to their prespecified time periods, while time-to-event outcomes incorporated varying follow-up through survival analysis.

## 8 Regression models

Regression blocks:
  
- Block 1: technique effect on postoperative outcomes (complications, readmissions, reoperation, VUR and UTI recurrence)
- Block 2: exposure-effect analysis (stent, operative time, catheterization) on postoperative outcomes
- Block 3: Prognostic factors for readmission and reoperation: Complications and VUR/UTI recurrence effects on readmissions and reoperation

REC011 (Binary outcome)  
POSTUTI (Time-to-event outcome)


After ATO weighting, your model is not really a conventional "univariable analysis." 
It is better described as:
"Weighted marginal treatment effect estimation using GEE." Because the confounding control occurred during weighting, not regression adjustment.


Multiple comparison correction is not dependent on the type of regression model. It is applied to the set of p-values that you consider part of the same family of hypotheses.


- Why AUC is not commonly reported for causal models
AUC is mainly used for:
  - clinical prediction models
- risk scores
- diagnostic models

Examples:
"Can we predict which child will develop postoperative obstruction?"
For those models, discrimination is the goal.

Your question is:
"Does Cohen vs Lich–Gregoir change the risk of postoperative obstruction/pain?"
Here, prediction performance is secondary.


- For a randomized trial or comparative effectiveness observational study, reviewers usually expect:
  - balance diagnostics,
  - confounder selection rationale,
  - sensitivity analyses,
not AUC.

Reporting AUC may confuse the interpretation:
A reviewer may ask:
"Are you developing a prediction model or estimating a causal effect?"

### Block 1

```{r reg1w}

# GEE model after overlap weighting - Accounting for center-clustering

# Block 1: technique effect on postoperative outcomes = Univariable analyses

# Question: What is the difference in outcome risk between techniques among patients who could have received either technique?" -> This includes all pathways through which technique may influence outcomes. For example: TRT2→STENT→UTI is included in the treatment effect.

outcomes <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365",
  "REC011",
  "REC011_best",
  "REC011_worst"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
Out[outcomes] <- lapply(
  Out[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Apply GEE model after overlap weighting for all binary outcomes
gee_results <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2")
  )
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = Out,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results) <- outcomes


# Combine results into one table
gee_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results[[x]]
    tmp <- tmp %>%
      filter(grepl("^TRT2", term)) %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
    tmp
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table
gee_table_final <- gee_table %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = p.value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )

# the warnings are a consequence of valid ATO weighting, not an error. Your models ran successfully.
# The model internally detects that the weighted outcome contribution is fractional and gives the warning.
# You are not using frequency weights to represent replicated patients. You are using sampling/analysis weights from propensity score overlap weighting to create a pseudo-population.
# With propensity score weighting, fractional contributions are expected.


# weighted Cox model for POSTUTI

# The main issue with the clustered Cox model (using survey design object with  ids = CENTER) was the unstable variance estimation from only four clusters (a higher number of clusters is required).

cox_uti <- svycoxph(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2 + strata(CENTER),
  design = design_ato
)

# your earlier binary GEE models are estimating a population-average effect, while this stratified Cox model estimates a center-stratified Cox effect. This difference is acceptable, but you should describe both as center-adjusted analyses rather than claiming they are exactly identical estimands.

# If you wanted HRs for each center, you would need: + factor(CENTER)

# `strata(CENTER)` allows each center to have its own baseline hazard function. It estimates the treatment effect adjusted for different baseline hazards across centers.

cox_summary <- summary(cox_uti)

cox_row <- grep(
  "^TRT2",
  rownames(cox_summary$coefficients)
)

POSTUTI_table <- data.frame(
  Outcome = "POSTUTI",
  Effect_measure = "HR",
  Estimate = sprintf(
    "%.2f",
    cox_summary$coefficients[
      cox_row,
      "exp(coef)"
    ]
  ),
  CI = paste0(
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summary$conf.int[cox_row, "lower .95"]),
    "–",
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summary$conf.int[cox_row, "upper .95"])
  ),
  P_value = cox_summary$coefficients[
    cox_row,
    "Pr(>|z|)"
  ]
)

# Combine final results
final_results <- rbind(
  gee_table_final,
  POSTUTI_table
)


# Multiple correction

## Bonferroni correction
final_results$p_bonferroni <- p.adjust(
  final_results$P_value,
  method = "bonferroni"
)

## Holm-Bonferroni
final_results$p_holm <- p.adjust(
  final_results$P_value,
  method = "holm"
)

## Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
final_results$p_FDR <- p.adjust(
  final_results$P_value,
  method = "BH"
)


final_results <- final_results %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(P_value, p_bonferroni, p_holm, p_FDR),
      ~case_when(
        .x < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)
      )
    )
  )

final_results

final_results %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/treatment_unadj_w.docx"
  )


# Evaluate whether CENTER distribution is balanced after weighting, despite that CENTER was not included in weighting

# bal.tab(
#   w.out,
#   data = Out,
#   addl = ~ CENTER
# )

# Results showed that all CENTER SMD < 0.05 → excellent balance
# Therefore, after ATO weighting, CENTER is well balanced between treatment groups.
# This is an important finding because your original data showed strong center-treatment imbalance.
# Why did CENTER become balanced although it was not in the propensity score model?
# This is possible because CENTER was correlated with the covariates you included in the propensity model.
```

```{r reg2aw}
# Block 2: exposure-effect analysis (stent, operative time, catheterization) on postoperative outcomes = Multivariable analyses


# Question: Is there still an association between technique and outcome after accounting for differences in procedural management?  --> This is closer to a direct effect of technique.


# Catheterization duration was considered a post-treatment variable and was not included in the outcome models to avoid adjustment for a potential mediator of the association between surgical technique and postoperative outcomes. Stent placement and operative time were retained as procedural characteristics that may influence postoperative outcomes and may account for differences in perioperative management and technical complexity between surgical approaches (and case complexity).

# Operative time was included in secondary analyses as a procedural characteristic reflecting both technical aspects of the surgical approach and operative complexity.

# Final decision: I will remove OPRTIME from multivariable models.

# Your justification for keeping STENT is relatively strong:
## The literature recognizes stent use as a variable component of ureteral reimplantation technique.
## Stent placement may directly influence postoperative outcomes (e.g., obstruction, urinary symptoms, UTI, discomfort).
## It may represent a modifiable aspect of perioperative management.


# When you adjust for OPRTIME, you are asking: "Among patients with the same operative duration, is there still a difference between techniques?"

  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",

  "ILEUS",

)

)

   )

})
```

```{r reg2aw_norec}
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
Out[outcomes] <- lapply(
  Out[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Predictors to include in the outcome models
predictors <- c("TRT2", "STENT")


# Apply GEE model after overlap weighting for all binary outcomes
gee_results <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~",
          paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")
   )
  )  
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = Out,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results) <- outcomes

# Combine results into one table
gee_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results[[x]]
    tmp %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table
gee_table_final <- gee_table %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = p.value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Predictor = term,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )

# the warnings are a consequence of valid ATO weighting, not an error. Your models ran successfully.
# The model internally detects that the weighted outcome contribution is fractional and gives the warning.
# You are not using frequency weights to represent replicated patients. You are using sampling/analysis weights from propensity score overlap weighting to create a pseudo-population.
# With propensity score weighting, fractional contributions are expected.


# weighted Cox model for POSTUTI

# The main issue with the clustered Cox model (using survey design object with  ids = CENTER) was the unstable variance estimation from only four clusters (a higher number of clusters is required).

cox_uti <- svycoxph(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2 + STENT  + strata(CENTER),
  design = design_ato
)

# your earlier binary GEE models are estimating a population-average effect, while this stratified Cox model estimates a center-stratified Cox effect. This difference is acceptable, but you should describe both as center-adjusted analyses rather than claiming they are exactly identical estimands.

# If you wanted HRs for each center, you would need: + factor(CENTER)

# `strata(CENTER)` allows each center to have its own baseline hazard function. It estimates the treatment effect adjusted for different baseline hazards across centers.

cox_summary <- summary(cox_uti)

cox_row <- rownames(cox_summary$coefficients)

POSTUTI_table <- data.frame(
  Outcome = "POSTUTI",
  Predictor = rownames(cox_summary$coefficients),
  Effect_measure = "HR",
  Estimate = sprintf(
    "%.2f",
    cox_summary$coefficients[
      cox_row,
      "exp(coef)"
    ]
  ),
  CI = paste0(
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summary$conf.int[cox_row, "lower .95"]),
    "–",
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summary$conf.int[cox_row, "upper .95"])
  ),
  P_value = cox_summary$coefficients[
    cox_row,
    "Pr(>|z|)"
  ]
)


# Combine final results
final_results <- rbind(
  gee_table_final,
  POSTUTI_table
)


final_results

final_results <- final_results %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(P_value),
      ~case_when(
        .x < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)
      )
    )
  )


final_results %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
```

### Block 2ai - without VUR recurrence + with interaction (to calculate OR for two levels) (secondary effect-modification analysis)

```{r}

## Manual calculation

outcomes <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365"
)

# Convert outcomes to numeric
Out[outcomes] <- lapply(
  Out[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)


# Function to extract treatment effects within each stent stratum
get_gee_interaction_results <- function(y) {
  
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2 * STENT")
  )
  
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = Out,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  
  # Coefficients
  beta <- coef(model)
  
  # Robust covariance matrix
  V <- vcov(model)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among NO-STENT patients
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_no_stent <- beta["TRT21"]
  
  se_no_stent <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"]
  )
  
  OR_no_stent <- exp(b_no_stent)
  
  CI_no_stent <- exp(
    b_no_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_no_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among STENTED patients
  # = TRT21 + TRT21:STENT1
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_stent <- beta["TRT21"] +
    beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  # Variance of the linear combination:
  # Var(beta1 + beta3)
  
  var_stent <-
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"] +
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"] +
    2 * V["TRT21", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_stent <- sqrt(var_stent)
  
  OR_stent <- exp(b_stent)
  
  CI_stent <- exp(
    b_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Interaction test
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_interaction <- beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_interaction <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  )
  
  z_interaction <- b_interaction / se_interaction
  
  p_interaction <- 2 * pnorm(
    abs(z_interaction),
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Return manuscript-ready results
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  data.frame(
    Outcome = y,
    
    `LG vs Cohen, No Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_no_stent,
        CI_no_stent[1],
        CI_no_stent[2]
      ),
    
    `LG vs Cohen, Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_stent,
        CI_stent[1],
        CI_stent[2]
      ),
    
    P_interaction = p_interaction,
    
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# Run for all 8 outcomes
interaction_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(outcomes, get_gee_interaction_results)
)


interaction_results



# POSTUTI

cox_uti <- svycoxph(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2 * STENT +
    strata(CENTER),
  design = design_ato
)

# Coefficients
beta_cox <- coef(cox_uti)

# Covariance matrix
V_cox <- vcov(cox_uti)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# LG vs Cohen among NO-STENT patients
# -------------------------------------------------------

b_no_stent_cox <- beta_cox["TRT21"]

se_no_stent_cox <- sqrt(
  V_cox["TRT21", "TRT21"]
)

HR_no_stent <- exp(b_no_stent_cox)

CI_no_stent_cox <- exp(
  b_no_stent_cox +
    c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_no_stent_cox
)


# -------------------------------------------------------
# LG vs Cohen among STENTED patients
# = TRT21 + TRT21:STENT1
# -------------------------------------------------------

b_stent_cox <- beta_cox["TRT21"] +
  beta_cox["TRT21:STENT1"]

var_stent_cox <-
  V_cox["TRT21", "TRT21"] +
  V_cox["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"] +
  2 * V_cox["TRT21", "TRT21:STENT1"]

se_stent_cox <- sqrt(var_stent_cox)

HR_stent <- exp(b_stent_cox)

CI_stent_cox <- exp(
  b_stent_cox +
    c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_stent_cox
)


# -------------------------------------------------------
# Interaction p-value
# -------------------------------------------------------

b_interaction_cox <- beta_cox["TRT21:STENT1"]

se_interaction_cox <- sqrt(
  V_cox["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"]
)

z_interaction_cox <-
  b_interaction_cox / se_interaction_cox

p_interaction_cox <- 2 * pnorm(
  abs(z_interaction_cox),
  lower.tail = FALSE
)


# Create POSTUTI result
POSTUTI_interaction <- data.frame(
  Outcome = "POSTUTI",
  
  `LG vs Cohen, No Stent` =
    sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
      HR_no_stent,
      CI_no_stent_cox[1],
      CI_no_stent_cox[2]
    ),
  
  `LG vs Cohen, Stent` =
    sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
      HR_stent,
      CI_stent_cox[1],
      CI_stent_cox[2]
    ),
  
  P_interaction = p_interaction_cox
)

POSTUTI_interaction


```

```{r reg2bw}
  ),
  P_value = cox_summary$coefficients[
    cox_row,
    "Pr(>|z|)"
  ]
)
```

### Block 3

```{r reg3w}

# Block 3: Prognostic factors for readmission and reoperation = Multivariable analyses including (Treatment + perioperative exposure + one complication)


# IMPORTANT: The model is valid statistically, but interpretation depends on whether the complication precedes the outcome. / we may need to discard GU30.

# Your analysis seems to be asking: "Are postoperative complications associated with subsequent outcomes (GU30, GU90, PROC365)?" In this case, correcting within outcome is defensible because each outcome represents a separate hypothesis family.

# Multiplicity adjustment was performed separately for each prespecified outcome because outcomes represented distinct clinically relevant time horizons.

# Why temporality is an issue: For a predictor to be a causal risk factor, it must occur before the outcome. Therefore, the logistic regression estimate (example: A model: GU90 ~ POSTUTI) does not estimate: "UTI causes readmission." Instead, it estimates: "Patients who experienced postoperative UTI at any time during follow-up had different odds of readmission within 90 days compared with patients without postoperative UTI." This is an association between two postoperative events. That is a valid secondary analysis in retrospective surgical studies.


# A limitation for this analysis: "Because exact timing of postoperative complications was not available, temporal relationships between complications and subsequent healthcare utilization could not always be established. Therefore, these analyses should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects."

# As the change of reversed temporality is higher with GU30, I would restrict the analysis to GU90 and PROC365.


# Outcomes to be explained
outcomes <- c(
  "GU90",
  "PROC365"
)

# Complications evaluated separately
complications <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "POSTUTI",         # here, no cox regression because the outcome is binary and POSTUTI is an exposure
  "REC011",  
  "REC011_best",
  "REC011_worst"
)

# Adjustment variables
adjusters <- c(
  "TRT2",
  "STENT"
)


# Convert binary variables to numeric
Out[c(outcomes, complications)] <- lapply(
  Out[c(outcomes, complications)],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)


gee_results <- list()

for (outcome in outcomes) {
  
  for (complication in complications) {
    
    print(paste("Running:", outcome, complication))
    
    vars <- c(
      outcome,
      complication,
      adjusters,
      "CENTER",
      "weights"
    )
    
    data_model <- Out %>%
      dplyr::select(all_of(vars)) %>%
      na.omit()
    
    formula <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~",
        paste(
          c(complication, adjusters),
          collapse = " + "
        )
      )
    )
    
    model <- geeglm(
      formula,
      data = data_model,
      id = CENTER,
      weights = weights,
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      corstr = "exchangeable"
    )
    
    result <- tidy(
      model,
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      conf.int = TRUE
    ) %>%
      filter(term == complication) %>%
      mutate(
        Outcome = outcome,
        Predictor = complication,
        N = nrow(data_model)        
      )
    
    gee_results[[paste(outcome, complication, sep="_")]] <- result
  }
}


gee_table <- bind_rows(gee_results)


gee_table_final <- gee_table %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = p.value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome,
    Predictor,
    N,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )

gee_table_final <- gee_table_final %>%
  group_by(Outcome) %>%
  mutate(
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(
      P_value,
      method = "bonferroni"
    ),
    p_holm = p.adjust(
      P_value,
      method = "holm"
    ),
    p_FDR = p.adjust(
      P_value,
      method = "BH"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



gee_table_final <- gee_table_final %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(P_value, p_bonferroni, p_holm, p_FDR),
      ~case_when(
        .x < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)
      )
    )
  )


# GU90 table
gee_table_final %>%
  filter(Outcome == "GU90") %>%
  dplyr::select(-Outcome) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("N", "Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/GU90_adj_weighted.docx"
  )


# PROC365 table
gee_table_final %>%
  filter(Outcome == "PROC365") %>%
  dplyr::select(-Outcome) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("N","Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/PROC365_adj_weighted.docx"
  )
```

# PAIN - Non-epidural Cohort

Here, we estimated: Effect of surgical technique on pain in the overlap population of children who were not given epidural.

Above: we estimated: Effect of surgical technique on other outcomes in the overlap population of all children.

Whenever the target population changes because of an inclusion/exclusion criterion, the propensity score model should generally be re-estimated.

Overlap weighting only guarantees balance in the population on which the propensity score was estimated. Once you remove observations after weighting, that guarantee disappears -> The correct approach is to restrict the cohort first and then estimate a new propensity score model and new ATO (overlap) weights within that restricted cohort.

In your case, the scientific question is:
Among children who did not receive epidural injection, does surgical technique affect postoperative pain?

This is not the same estimand as:
Among all children, what is the effect of surgical technique?

### 1 Filter & weight the new population

```{r filterpain}

# Filter dataset to only those who did not receive EPIDURAL
Outp <- Out %>%
  filter(EPIDURAL == "0") %>%
  mutate(
    PAIN = factor(
      PAIN,
      levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3"),
      labels = c(
        "No pain",
        "Mild pain (score 1-3)",
        "Moderate pain (score 4-6)",
        "Severe pain (score 7-10)"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# Do weighting: using ATO (Recommended)

set.seed(123)

w.outp <- weightit(
  TRT2 ~ AGS + YEARS + GENDER + BMI + PREOPRNPLN + HISTOINJ +
    SURGIND2 + PREOPVURGRADE + VURSIDE + UDR7M + VURPHASE +
    PREOPEPISODE1 + PREOPTYPEU1 + PREOPRNSCR + SURGTECH2,
  data = Outp,
  method = "ps",
  estimand = "ATO", 
  stabilize = FALSE  # used in ATE
)
Outp$weights <- w.outp$weights  # Add weights to the dataset
write.csv(Outp, "data/weighted_nonepidural_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

summary(w.outp$weights)


# Table for balance
# This gives: SMD before and after weighting, and flagged imbalance (>0.1)
balp <- cobalt::bal.tab(w.outp, un = TRUE, ESS = TRUE, m.threshold = 0.1)  # ESS to calculate ESS separately by treatment group
# un=TRUE shows imbalance before AND after weighting, un=FALSE shows only after weighting
balp 

balp_df <- as.data.frame(balp$Balance)
smd_table <- balp_df %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = rownames(balp_df),
    SMD_Before = round(abs(Diff.Un), 3),
    SMD_After  = round(abs(Diff.Adj), 3)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, SMD_Before, SMD_After) # SMDs for each covariate individually, before and after weighting, I specify the use of selct from dplyr library because there is another package's select() function from MASS library

smd_table %>%
  flextable() %>%
  save_as_docx(path = "output/SMD_pw.docx")


# Figure for balance - Love plot
# Review guidelines to decide on plotting Standardized or Absolute Mean Differences
plp <- love.plot(
  w.outp,
  threshold = 0.1,
  abs = TRUE, # As SMD sign is meaningless for balance, show only absolute SMDs using abs = TRUE (the correct interpretation of SMD): Because SMD direction (+/-) is meaningless, only magnitude matters
  stats = "mean.diffs",       # forces SMD instead of raw differences
  var.order = "unadjusted",   # Orders variables based on imbalance before matching
  drop.distance = TRUE,      # To exclude the distance from the plot
  sample.names = c("Before Overlap Weighting", "After Overlap Weighting"),
    var.names = c(
    AGS = "Age at surgery",
    YEARS = "Year of surgery",
    BMI = "Body mass index",
    GENDER = "Female gender",
    PREOPRNPLN = "Preop pyelonephritis",
    HISTOINJ = "History of injection",
    VURSIDE = "Right-sided VUR",
    UDR7M = "Ureteral dilation ≥ 7mm",
    PREOPTYPEU1 = "Preop febrile UTIs",
    PREOPRNSCR = "Preop renal scarring",
    VURPHASE_1 = "Reflux: voiding phase",
    VURPHASE_2 = "Reflux: filling phase",
    VURPHASE_3 = "Reflux: filling + voiding",
    SURGTECH2_1 = "Surgeon experience ≥100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_2 = "Surgeon experience 50-100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_3 = "Surgeon experience <50 operations",
    PREOPEPISODE1_1 = "Preop UTI episodes: 1",
    PREOPEPISODE1_2 = "Preop UTI episodes: 2",
    PREOPEPISODE1_3 = "Preop UTI episodes: ≥3",
    SURGIND2_1 = "Indication: breakthrough UTI",
    SURGIND2_2 = "Indication: high-grade reflux (III-V)",
    SURGIND2_3 = "Indication: poor compliance to medical treatment",
    SURGIND2_4 = "Indication: ineffective/poorly tolerated CAP",
    SURGIND2_5 = "Indication: other",
    PREOPVURGRADE_3 = "Preop VUR grade: III",
    PREOPVURGRADE_4 = "Preop VUR grade: IV",
    PREOPVURGRADE_5 = "Preop VUR grade: V"
  )
  )

plp <- plp +
    labs(
    x = "Absolute Standardized Differences",
    subtitle = "Overlap population of children who did not receive epidural analgesia"
  )
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      panel.background = element_blank(), 
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.3, "cm"),
      panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
   )

ggsave ("figures/love_plot_pw.png", plot = plp, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)

# Compute mean SMD
smdp_df <- balp$Balance
mean_smdp_before <- mean(abs(smdp_df$Diff.Un), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before matching
mean_smdp_after <- mean(abs(smdp_df$Diff.Adj), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before matching
mean_smdp <- data.frame(
  Mean_SMDp_Before = mean_smdp_before,
  Mean_SMDp_After = mean_smdp_after
)

mean_smdp
```

### 2 Descriptive analysis

```{r painw}

# Baseline characteristics in the population for pain
table1p<- Outp %>%
  dplyr::select(YEARS, AGS, GENDER, BMI, HISTOINJ, SURGIND2, PREOPVURGRADE, VURSIDE, UDR7M, 
         VURPHASE, PREOPTYPEU1, PREOPEPISODE1, PREOPRNPLN, PREOPRNSCR,
         SURGTECH2, CENTER, TRT2
  ) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = TRT2,  # for stratification
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}-{p75})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)" 
    ),
    digits = all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1),  # n = 0 decimals, p = 1 decimal
    missing = "ifany",  # shows missing only when present
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  add_p(pvalue_fun = ~style_pvalue(.x, digits = 3)) %>%  #  3 decimals 
  bold_labels()
```

### 4 Regression

```{r regpain}

# As PAIN is an ordinal variable -> Ordinal logistic GEE model is appropriate but ordinal logistic GEE did not support weighting, so I will transform Pain to a binary outcome

# PAIN will not be added to the first set of hypothesis because:
## Set 1: Main postoperative outcomes (full cohort)
## Set 2: Pain outcomes (non-epidural population)


# Because postoperative pain was evaluated among children who did not receive epidural analgesia, a separate overlap-weighted analysis was performed within this subgroup. Multiple comparisons were therefore handled separately for pain outcomes and other postoperative outcomes.

# After overlap weighting, Lich–Gregoir was associated with 80% lower odds of severe postoperative pain compared with Cohen (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.15–0.26).


# -----------------------------------------
### Moderate-severe pain vs. Other levels
# -----------------------------------------

Outp <- Outp %>%
  mutate(
    PAIN_ms = factor(
      ifelse(
        PAIN %in% c(
          "Moderate pain (score 4-6)",
          "Severe pain (score 7-10)"
        ),
        1,
        0
      ),
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c(
        "No/Mild pain (score 0-3)",
        "Moderate-Severe pain (score 4-10)"
      )
    )
  )


Outp$PAIN_ms <- ifelse(
  Outp$PAIN_ms == "Moderate-Severe pain (score 4-10)",
  1,
  0
)

# -----------------------------------------------------
### Exploratory analysis: Severe pain vs. Other levels
# -----------------------------------------------------

Outp <- Outp %>%
  mutate(
    PAIN_s = factor(
      ifelse(
        PAIN == "Severe pain (score 7-10)",
        1,
        0
      ),
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c(
        "No severe pain (score 0-6)",
        "Severe pain (score 7-10)"
      )
    )
  )

# a numeric binary outcome:
Outp$PAIN_s <- ifelse(
  Outp$PAIN_s == "Severe pain (score 7-10)",
  1,
  0
)

#----------
# Block 1

  "PAIN_ms",
  "PAIN_s"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
Outp[outcomes] <- lapply(
  Outp[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Apply GEE model after overlap weighting for all binary outcomes
gee_results <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2")
  )
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = Outp,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results) <- outcomes


# Combine results into one table
gee_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results[[x]]
    tmp <- tmp %>%
      filter(grepl("^TRT2", term)) %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
    tmp
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table

  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",

    ),

#------------------------
# Block 2ai- Interaction
#------------------------

outcomes <- c(
  "PAIN_ms",
  "PAIN_s"
)


# convert outcomes to numeric
Outp[outcomes] <- lapply(
  Outp[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Function to extract treatment effects within each stent stratum
get_gee_interaction_results <- function(y) {
  
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2 * STENT")
  )
  
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = Outp,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  
  # Coefficients
  beta <- coef(model)
  
  # Robust covariance matrix
  V <- vcov(model)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among NO-STENT patients
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_no_stent <- beta["TRT21"]
  
  se_no_stent <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"]
  )
  
  OR_no_stent <- exp(b_no_stent)
  
  CI_no_stent <- exp(
    b_no_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_no_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among STENTED patients
  # = TRT21 + TRT21:STENT1
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_stent <- beta["TRT21"] +
    beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  # Variance of the linear combination:
  # Var(beta1 + beta3)
  
  var_stent <-
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"] +
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"] +
    2 * V["TRT21", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_stent <- sqrt(var_stent)
  
  OR_stent <- exp(b_stent)
  
  CI_stent <- exp(
    b_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Interaction test
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_interaction <- beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_interaction <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  )
  
  z_interaction <- b_interaction / se_interaction
  
  p_interaction <- 2 * pnorm(
    abs(z_interaction),
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Return manuscript-ready results
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  data.frame(
    Outcome = y,
    
    `LG vs Cohen, No Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_no_stent,
        CI_no_stent[1],
        CI_no_stent[2]
      ),
    
    `LG vs Cohen, Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_stent,
        CI_stent[1],
        CI_stent[2]
      ),
    
    P_interaction = p_interaction,
    
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# Run for all 8 outcomes
interaction_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(outcomes, get_gee_interaction_results)
)


interaction_results
```

```{r evalue}
# Specify rare outcome assumption
evalue_data <- evalue_data %>%
  mutate(
    rare = ifelse(
      Outcome %in% c("SURG", "GU90", "SURGadj", "GU90adj", "REC011_worstadj", "GU30adj", "Pain_ms", "Pain_s", "Pain_msadj", "Pain_sadj"),
      FALSE,
      TRUE
    )
  )


# Calculate E-values
evalue_results <- evalue_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    OR_input = ifelse(OR < 1, 1/OR, OR),
    CI_low_input = ifelse(OR < 1, 1/CI_high, CI_low),
    CI_high_input = ifelse(OR < 1, 1/CI_low, CI_high),
    
    E_value = list(
      evalues.OR(
        est = OR_input,
        lo = CI_low_input,
        hi = CI_high_input,
        rare = rare
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

evalue_table <- evalue_results %>%
  mutate(
    E_value_point = sapply(
      E_value,
      function(x) x["E-values", "point"]
    ),
    E_value_CI = sapply(
      E_value,
      function(x) x["E-values", "lower"]
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome,
    OR,
    CI_low,
    CI_high,
    E_value_point,
    E_value_CI
  )

evalue_table


evalue_table_formatted <- evalue_table %>%
  mutate(
    OR = sprintf("%.2f", OR),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", CI_low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", CI_high)
    ),
    E_value_point = sprintf("%.2f", E_value_point),
    E_value_CI = sprintf("%.2f", E_value_CI)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome,
    OR,
    CI,
    E_value_point,
    E_value_CI
  )

evalue_table_formatted %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("OR", "CI", "E_value_point", "E_value_CI"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/E_value_stent.docx"
  )


## The E-value answers: How strong would an unmeasured confounder need to be associated with both the exposure and the outcome (on the risk ratio scale) to fully explain away the observed association?
# For example: E-value = 6.88
# Interpretation: An unmeasured confounder would need to be associated with both the treatment and obstructive ureteral complications by a risk ratio of at least 6.88 (above and beyond measured covariates) to explain away the observed association.

## Rosenbaum's sensitivity analysis addresses a slightly different question: How strong would an unmeasured variable have to influence treatment assignment to change the conclusion of the analysis?
# The key parameter is Γ (Gamma). For example: Γ = 10 → very robust
# Interpretation: An unmeasured confounder would need to increase the odds of treatment assignment by 10-fold to make the result non-significant.

# There is no universal rule that says "calculate E-values only for significant unadjusted outcomes" or "only for significant adjusted outcomes." The decision should be based on which estimates represent your main scientific conclusions.

# For our study, Report E-values for adjusted treatment effects of clinically important outcomes, regardless of whether significant or not.
```

#### 1.1. Plot E-value

```{r evalueplot}

# E-value sensitivity contour plot for Obstruction risk in overlap weighting before adjustment to procedural factors


# OBST values
RR_est <- 3.67
RR_CI  <- 2.21

E_value_point <- RR_est + sqrt(RR_est*(RR_est-1))
E_value_CI <- RR_CI + sqrt(RR_CI*(RR_CI-1))

# Function for contour
evalue_curve <- function(RR){

  x <- seq(RR + 0.001, 20, length.out = 5000)

  y <- RR * (x - 1)/(x - RR)

  data.frame(
    RR_EU = x,
    RR_UY = y
  )
}

curve_est <- evalue_curve(RR_est)
curve_CI  <- evalue_curve(RR_CI)


# Create plot
evalue_plot <- ggplot() +

  # Point estimate curve
  geom_line(
    data = curve_est,
    aes(
      x = RR_EU,
      y = RR_UY
    ),
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  # CI curve
  geom_line(
    data = curve_CI,
    aes(
      x = RR_EU,
      y = RR_UY
    ),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  # E-value point
  geom_point(
    aes(
      x = E_value_point,
      y = E_value_point
    ),
    color = "red",
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  # CI E-value point
  geom_point(
    aes(
      x = E_value_CI,
      y = E_value_CI
    ),
    color = "blue",
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  # Labels
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = E_value_point,
    y = E_value_point + 0.35,
    label = paste0(
      "E value: (",
      round(E_value_point,2),
      ", ",
      round(E_value_point,2),
      ")"
    ),
    color = "black",
    size = 4,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  annotate(
    "text",
    x = E_value_CI,
    y = E_value_CI - 0.25,
    label = paste0(
      "E value (CI): (",
      round(E_value_CI,2),
      ", ",
      round(E_value_CI,2),
      ")"
    ),
    color = "black",
    size = 4,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1,20),
    breaks = seq(5,20,5)
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(1,20),
    breaks = seq(0,20,5)
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Risk ratio for exposure-confounder relationship",
    y = "Risk ratio for confounder-outcome relationship"
  ) +

  theme_gray(base_size = 14)
```

# SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS 2

### 1 Do matching 1:1 without replacement

```{r matching, warning=FALSE}

# Fit matching model using propensity score (calculated inside MatchIt): 1:1 matching

set.seed(123) # Fixes the sequence of "random" operations = the same individuals are matched every time
 
m.out <- matchit(
  TRT2 ~ AGS + YEARS + GENDER + BMI + PREOPRNPLN + HISTOINJ +
    SURGIND2 + PREOPVURGRADE + VURSIDE + UDR7M + VURPHASE +
    PREOPEPISODE1 + PREOPTYPEU1 + PREOPRNSCR + SURGTECH2,
  data = Out,
  method = "nearest",
  ratio = 1,  # 1:1 matching (1 treated : 1 control)
  distance = "logit",
# caliper should be a numeric value in MatchIt
# This means: 0.2 SD of the logit of PS (MatchIt interprets correctly)
   caliper = 0.2   # A caliper = maximum allowed distance between treated and control PS = 0.2 (Austin 2011)
) # When the variance of the linear propensity score in the treatment group is twice as large as that in the control group, a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations removes 98% of the bias in a normally distributed covariate. If the variance in the treatment group is much larger than that in the control group, smaller calipers are necessary.


mdata <- match.data(
  m.out,
  weights = "weights_psm" # give a new name for the matching weights because the original dataset Out already contains a variable named weights from the previous overlap weighting analysis.
)
# Extract the matched dataset with columns: distance(PS), weights, subclass
# weights = how much each matched subject contributes in analysis
# In 1:1 matching, weights usually = 1
# you can ignore weights in further analysis, but using them is safer and more standard
# glm(outcome ~ TRT2, data = mdata, weights = weights) (standard) or glm(outcome ~ TRT2, data = mdata)

readr::write_csv(mdata, "data/matched_data.csv")  
# write.csv() = base R, simple, works everywhere: write.csv(mdata, file = "data/matched_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
# write_csv() = modern, faster, cleaner, recommended for research workflows 


# Table for balance
# This gives: SMD before and after matching, and flagged imbalance (>0.1)
balm <- cobalt::bal.tab(m.out, un = TRUE, m.threshold = 0.1)  
# un=TRUE shows imbalance before AND after matching, un=FALSE shows only after matching
balm 

bal_dfm <- as.data.frame(balm$Balance)
smd_tablem <- bal_dfm %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = rownames(bal_dfm),
    SMD_Before = round(abs(Diff.Un), 3),
    SMD_After  = round(abs(Diff.Adj), 3)
  ) %>%
  select(Variable, SMD_Before, SMD_After) # SMDs for each covariate individually, before and after matching

smd_tablem %>%
  flextable() %>%
  save_as_docx(path = "output/SMD_psm.docx")


# how much effective sample size remains (overall ESS: calculated manually)?
summary(m.out$weights)
bal.tab(m.out)$Effective.Sample.Size
sum(m.out$weights)^2 / sum(m.out$weights^2)


# Figure for balance - Love plot
# Review guidelines to decide on plotting Standardized or Absolute Mean Differences
plm <- love.plot(
  m.out,
  threshold = 0.1,
  abs = TRUE, # As SMD sign is meaningless for balance, show only absolute SMDs using abs = TRUE (the correct interpretation of SMD): Because SMD direction (+/-) is meaningless, only magnitude matters
  stats = "mean.diffs",       # forces SMD instead of raw differences
  var.order = "unadjusted",   # Orders variables based on imbalance before matching
  drop.distance = TRUE,      # To exclude the distance from the plot
  sample.names = c("Before matching", "After matching"),
    size = 4,
    var.names = c(
    AGS = "Age at surgery",
    YEARS = "Year of surgery",
    BMI = "Body mass index",
    GENDER = "Female gender",
    PREOPRNPLN = "Preop pyelonephritis",
    HISTOINJ = "History of injection",
    VURSIDE = "Right-sided VUR",
    UDR7M = "Ureteral dilation ≥ 7mm",
    PREOPTYPEU1 = "Preop febrile UTIs",
    PREOPRNSCR = "Preop renal scarring",
    VURPHASE_1 = "Reflux: voiding phase",
    VURPHASE_2 = "Reflux: filling phase",
    VURPHASE_3 = "Reflux: filling + voiding",
    SURGTECH2_1 = "Surgeon experience ≥100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_2 = "Surgeon experience 50-100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_3 = "Surgeon experience <50 operations",
    PREOPEPISODE1_1 = "Preop UTI episodes: 1",
    PREOPEPISODE1_2 = "Preop UTI episodes: 2",
    PREOPEPISODE1_3 = "Preop UTI episodes: ≥3",
    SURGIND2_1 = "Indication: breakthrough UTI",
    SURGIND2_2 = "Indication: high-grade reflux (III-V)",
    SURGIND2_3 = "Indication: poor compliance to medical treatment",
    SURGIND2_4 = "Indication: ineffective/poorly tolerated CAP",
    SURGIND2_5 = "Indication: other",
    PREOPVURGRADE_3 = "Preop VUR grade: III",
    PREOPVURGRADE_4 = "Preop VUR grade: IV",
    PREOPVURGRADE_5 = "Preop VUR grade: V"
  )
  )

plm <- plm +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Before matching" = "#0072B2",
      "After matching" = "#D55E00"
    )
     )+
    labs(
        x = "Absolute Standardized Differences",
      subtitle = "Matched population"
  ) +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      panel.background = element_blank(), 
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.3, "cm"),
      panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
   )

ggsave ("figures/love_plot_m.png", plot = plm, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)

#   "figures/love_plot.png",

# Note: A propensity score should include: only baseline variables measured before treatment assignment

# “Distance” in the Love plot is the propensity score itself, included to show how well matching balanced the overall treatment assignment mechanism.
# Reviewers mainly check:
## All covariates < 0.1 after matching
## Distance reduced substantially
## Visual improvement in Love plot
# many papers exclude distance because: It is not a confounder, it is a derived variable, it often has very large pre-match imbalance (can visually dominate plot), it adds little clinical interpretation


# Compute mean SMD
smd_df_m <- balm$Balance
mean_smd_before_m <- mean(abs(smd_df_m$Diff.Un), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before matching
mean_smd_after_m <- mean(abs(smd_df_m$Diff.Adj), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before matching
mean_smd_m <- data.frame(

  Mean_SMD_After = mean_smd_after_m
)

mean_smd_m

# Best reporting practices
```

```{r descriptivem, warning=FALSE}
table3m

######## Postoperative UTI outcome as time-to-event outcome: Weighted survival curve
fit_psm <- survfit(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ Treatment,
  data = mdata
)

logrank_test <- survdiff(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2,
  data = mdata
)

p_value <- 1 - pchisq(
  logrank_test$chisq,
  df = length(logrank_test$n) - 1
)

p_label <- paste0("Log-rank test p = ", format.pval(p_value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001))

p_u_psm <- ggsurvplot(
  fit_psm,
  data = mdata,
  fun = "event",
  pval = p_label,
  pval.size = 4,
  pval.coord = c(0, 0.9),  #  c(x,y) according to my x and y scale
  conf.int = TRUE,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.y.text = FALSE,   # to remove text from y-axis in the risk table
  risk.table.fontsize = 4,   # controls numbers in table
  xlim = c(0,135),
  break.time.by = 12,
  xlab = "Follow-up time",
  ylab = "Cumulative incidence of postoperative symptomatic UTI",
  palette = c("#ADD8E6", "#00008B"),
  legend.title = "Treatment",
  legend.labs = c("Cohen Group", "Lich-Gregoir Group"),
  ylim = c(0,1)
)

#-----------------------
# Customize the plot
#-----------------------
p_u_psm$plot <- p_u_psm$plot +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 135),
    breaks = seq(0, 135, 12)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 100, 1), "%"),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  theme_classic() +   # Many clinical epidemiology journals prefer theme_classic() instead of theme_bw() as it automatically removes all gridlines
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 10)
  )

#----------------------------
# Customize the risk table
#----------------------------
p_u_psm$table <- p_u_psm$table +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 135),
    breaks = seq(0, 135, 12)
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y  = element_blank(),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 12),
    text         = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12)
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine plot and risk table
#------------------------------------------------------------
final_plot_psm <- p_u_psm$plot / p_u_psm$table +
  plot_layout(heights = c(4, 1))


#------------------------------------------------------------
# Save the figure
#------------------------------------------------------------
ggsave(
  filename = "figures/UTI_m.png",
  plot = final_plot_psm,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

# "In the propensity score-matched cohort, weighted Cox proportional hazards regression with robust variance estimation accounting for matched pairs was used to compare time to postoperative UTI."

# Figure: Weighted Kaplan–Meier cumulative incidence curves after matching.
# Table: Weighted Cox proportional hazards model using the matching weights estimating the association between surgical technique and time to postoperative UTI.


# Weighted Cox proportional hazards regression accounting for matched subclasses showed no significant difference in postoperative UTI risk between groups (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.54–1.42; p=0.592).
# If you show Kaplan–Meier curves: Survival distributions were compared using the log-rank test (p=0.60).


# Estimated 1-year survival
s_psm <- summary(fit_psm, times = 12, extend = TRUE)  # The extend = TRUE is useful if there isn't an event exactly at 365 days.

# Estimated 1-year cumulative probability of UTI
uti_1yr_psm <- data.frame(
  Treatment = s_psm$strata,
  UTI_1yr = 100 * (1 - s_psm$surv),
  Lower_95CI = 100 * (1 - s_psm$upper),
  Upper_95CI = 100 * (1 - s_psm$lower)
)

uti_1yr_psm
```

### 3 Regression

#### Block 1

```{r reg1m}

# GEE model after matching - Accounting for center-clustering

# Block 1: technique effect on postoperative outcomes = Univariable analyses

outcomes <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365",
  "REC011",
  "REC011_best",
  "REC011_worst"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
mdata[outcomes] <- lapply(
  mdata[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Apply GEE model after matching for all binary outcomes
gee_results_psm <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2")
  )
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = mdata,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights_psm,       # weights have no effect because weights are all equal
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results_psm) <- outcomes


# Combine results into one table
gee_table_psm <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results_psm), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results_psm[[x]]
    tmp <- tmp %>%
      filter(grepl("^TRT2", term)) %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
    tmp
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table
gee_table_final_psm <- gee_table_psm %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = p.value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )


# Cox model for POSTUTI: In the propensity score–matched cohort, Cox proportional hazards regression with robust standard errors accounting for matched pairs and stratification by center was performed to estimate the association between treatment and postoperative UTI.

cox_uti_psm <- coxph(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2 + strata(CENTER),
  data = mdata,
  weights = weights_psm,  # weights have no effect
  robust = TRUE,
  cluster = subclass   # after matching, data structure is: Each treated patient is paired with a control patient /Observations within a matched pair are not independent/The matched subclass (pair ID) defines the dependence structure.
)

# The interpretation is: Among patients with similar propensity scores (matched pairs), what is the association between surgical technique and time to postoperative UTI?

# `strata(CENTER)` allows each center to have its own baseline hazard function. It estimates the treatment effect adjusted for different baseline hazards across centers.

cox_summarypsm <- summary(cox_uti_psm)

cox_row <- grep(
  "^TRT2",
  rownames(cox_summarypsm$coefficients)
)

POSTUTI_table_psm <- data.frame(
  Outcome = "POSTUTI",
  Effect_measure = "HR",
  Estimate = sprintf(
    "%.2f",
    cox_summarypsm$coefficients[
      cox_row,
      "exp(coef)"
    ]
  ),
  CI = paste0(
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summarypsm$conf.int[cox_row, "lower .95"]),
    "–",
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summarypsm$conf.int[cox_row, "upper .95"])
  ),
  P_value = cox_summarypsm$coefficients[
    cox_row,
    "Pr(>|z|)"
  ]
)

# Combine final results
final_resultspsm <- rbind(
  gee_table_final_psm,
  POSTUTI_table_psm
)


# Multiple correction

## Bonferroni correction
final_resultspsm$p_bonferroni <- p.adjust(
  final_resultspsm$P_value,
  method = "bonferroni"
)

## Holm-Bonferroni
final_resultspsm$p_holm <- p.adjust(
  final_resultspsm$P_value,
  method = "holm"
)

## Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
final_resultspsm$p_FDR <- p.adjust(
  final_resultspsm$P_value,
  method = "BH"
)


final_resultspsm <- final_resultspsm %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(P_value, p_bonferroni, p_holm, p_FDR),
      ~case_when(
        .x < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)
      )
    )
  )

final_resultspsm

final_resultspsm %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/treatment_unadj_m.docx"
  )


# Evaluate whether CENTER distribution is balanced after weighting, despite that CENTER was not included in weighting

# bal.tab(
#  m.out,
#  data = Out,
#  addl = ~ CENTER
#)

# Results showed that all CENTER SMD < 0.05 → excellent balance
# Therefore, after ATO weighting, CENTER is well balanced between treatment groups.
# This is an important finding because your original data showed strong center-treatment imbalance.
# Why did CENTER become balanced although it was not in the propensity score model?
# This is possible because CENTER was correlated with the covariates you included in the propensity model.
```
