#### Block 2i2 - without VUR recurrence + with interaction (to calculate OR for two levels) (secondary effect-modification analysis)

```{r reg2m_norec}

# Block 2: exposure-effect analysis (stent, operative time, catheterization) on postoperative outcomes = Multivariable analyses

outcomes <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
mdata[outcomes] <- lapply(
  mdata[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)


# Apply GEE model after overlap weighting for all binary outcomes
get_gee_results_psm2 <- function(y) {
  
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2 * STENT")
  )
  
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = mdata,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights_psm,    # weights have no effect because weights are all equal
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  
  # Coefficients
  beta <- coef(model)
  
  # Robust covariance matrix
  V <- vcov(model)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among NO-STENT patients
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_no_stent <- beta["TRT21"]
  
  se_no_stent <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"]
  )
  
  OR_no_stent <- exp(b_no_stent)
  
  CI_no_stent <- exp(
    b_no_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_no_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among STENTED patients
  # = TRT21 + TRT21:STENT1
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_stent <- beta["TRT21"] +
    beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  # Variance of the linear combination:
  # Var(beta1 + beta3)
  
  var_stent <-
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"] +
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"] +
    2 * V["TRT21", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_stent <- sqrt(var_stent)
  
  OR_stent <- exp(b_stent)
  
  CI_stent <- exp(
    b_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Interaction test
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_interaction <- beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_interaction <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  )
  
  z_interaction <- b_interaction / se_interaction
  
  p_interaction <- 2 * pnorm(
    abs(z_interaction),
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Return manuscript-ready results
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  data.frame(
    Outcome = y,
    
    `LG vs Cohen, No Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_no_stent,
        CI_no_stent[1],
        CI_no_stent[2]
      ),
    
    `LG vs Cohen, Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_stent,
        CI_stent[1],
        CI_stent[2]
      ),
    
    P_interaction = p_interaction,
    
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# Run for all 8 outcomes
interaction_results_m <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(outcomes, get_gee_results_psm2)
)


interaction_results_m


# Cox model for POSTUTI

cox_uti_psm2 <- coxph(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2*STENT + strata(CENTER),
  data = mdata,
  weights = weights_psm,  # weights have no effect
  robust = TRUE,
  cluster = subclass   
)

# Coefficients
beta_cox <- coef(cox_uti_psm2)

# Covariance matrix
V_cox <- vcov(cox_uti_psm2)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# LG vs Cohen among NO-STENT patients
# -------------------------------------------------------

b_no_stent_cox <- beta_cox["TRT21"]

se_no_stent_cox <- sqrt(
  V_cox["TRT21", "TRT21"]
)

HR_no_stent <- exp(b_no_stent_cox)

CI_no_stent_cox <- exp(
  b_no_stent_cox +
    c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_no_stent_cox
)


# -------------------------------------------------------
# LG vs Cohen among STENTED patients
# = TRT21 + TRT21:STENT1
# -------------------------------------------------------

b_stent_cox <- beta_cox["TRT21"] +
  beta_cox["TRT21:STENT1"]

var_stent_cox <-
  V_cox["TRT21", "TRT21"] +
  V_cox["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"] +
  2 * V_cox["TRT21", "TRT21:STENT1"]

se_stent_cox <- sqrt(var_stent_cox)

HR_stent <- exp(b_stent_cox)

CI_stent_cox <- exp(
  b_stent_cox +
    c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_stent_cox
)


# -------------------------------------------------------
# Interaction p-value
# -------------------------------------------------------

b_interaction_cox <- beta_cox["TRT21:STENT1"]

se_interaction_cox <- sqrt(
  V_cox["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"]
)

z_interaction_cox <-
  b_interaction_cox / se_interaction_cox

p_interaction_cox <- 2 * pnorm(
  abs(z_interaction_cox),
  lower.tail = FALSE
)


# Create POSTUTI result

  Outcome = "POSTUTI",
  
  `LG vs Cohen, No Stent` =
    sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",

      CI_no_stent_cox[1],
      CI_no_stent_cox[2]
    ),
  
  `LG vs Cohen, Stent` =
    sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",

    ),

)
```

### 4 Rosenbaum's sensitivity analyses 

```{r rosenbaum}

# Rosenbaum's primal sensitivity analysis

outcomes <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365",
  "REC011",
  "REC011_best",
  "REC011_worst"
)

# Convert outcomes to numeric
mdata[outcomes] <- lapply(
  mdata[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)


# Function for Rosenbaum sensitivity analysis using rbounds
rosenbaum_binary <- function(outcome, data, match_object, 
                             gamma_seq = seq(1, 11, by = 0.1),
                            alpha = 0.05) {  
  
  # matched pairs
  treated_ids <- rownames(match_object$match.matrix)
  control_ids <- match_object$match.matrix[, 1]
  
  pairs <- data.frame(
    treated = data[treated_ids, outcome],
    control = data[control_ids, outcome]
  )
  
  # remove missing outcome pairs
  pairs <- na.omit(pairs)
  
  # discordant pairs
  # x = control has outcome, treated does not
  # y = treated has outcome, control does not
  x <- sum(pairs$control == 1 & pairs$treated == 0)
  y <- sum(pairs$treated == 1 & pairs$control == 0)
  
  # run Rosenbaum sensitivity
  if ((x + y) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      Outcome = outcome,
      Discordant_pairs = 0,
      x = x,
      y = y,
      p_Gamma1 = NA,
      gamma_max = NA,
      p_gamma_max = NA
    ))
  }
  
  # Run sensitivity over Gamma values

  gamma_results <- sapply(gamma_seq, function(g) {
    
  res <- binarysens(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      Gamma = g,
      GammaInc = 0.1  # GammaInc defines the increment used to increase Γ values when the function evaluates sensitivity.
    )

    # extract upper bound p-value corresponding to Gamma g
    res$bounds$`Upper bound`[
      res$bounds$Gamma == g
    ]
  })
  
    # p-value at Gamma = 1
    p_gamma1 <- gamma_results[gamma_seq == 1]
  
    # first Gamma where upper p-value >= alpha
    idx <- which(gamma_results < alpha)

if(length(idx) == 0){

  if(p_gamma1 >= alpha){
    
    gamma_max <- "NS at Gamma=1"
    p_gamma_max <- NA
    
  } else {
    
    gamma_max <- paste0(">=", max(gamma_seq))
    p_gamma_max <- gamma_results[length(gamma_results)]
    
  }

} else {
  
  gamma_max_value <- gamma_seq[max(idx)]
  
  # If still significant at the maximum tested Gamma
  if(gamma_max_value == max(gamma_seq)){
    
    gamma_max <- paste0(">=", max(gamma_seq))
    
  } else {
    
    gamma_max <- gamma_max_value
    
  }
  
  p_gamma_max <- gamma_results[max(idx)]
}

  # Extract p-values from rbounds object
  data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Discordant_pairs = x + y,
    x = x,
    y = y,
    p_Gamma1 = round(p_gamma1, 3),
    gamma_max = gamma_max,
    p_gamma_max = round(p_gamma_max, 3)
  )
}


# Run all outcomes
rosenbaum_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    outcomes,
    rosenbaum_binary,
    data = mdata,
    match_object = m.out
  )
)

rosenbaum_results


# Rename columns for publication
rosenbaum_results_pub <- rosenbaum_results %>%
  rename(
    Outcome = Outcome,
    `Discordant pairs` = Discordant_pairs,
    `Control only events (x)` = x,
    `Treated only events (y)` = y,
    `P-value (Γ=1)` = p_Gamma1,
    `Γmax` = gamma_max,
    `P-value at Γmax` = p_gamma_max
  )


# Create publication table
rosenbaum_table <- rosenbaum_results_pub %>%
  flextable() %>%
  
  # Add title
  add_header_lines(
    "Rosenbaum’s primal sensitivity analysis for postoperative outcomes in the matched cohort."
  ) %>%
  
  # Add footnote
  add_footer_lines(
    "The Gamma value Γ is a measure of sensitivity to hidden bias, representing the magnitude of differential odds of treatment assignment due to an unmeasured confounder that could alter the study conclusion. Γmax refers to the highest value of Γ for which the upper-bound p-value remained below 0.05. P-values correspond to the upper bound."
  ) %>%
  
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  
  align(
    j = c(
      "Discordant pairs",
      "Control only events (x)",
      "Treated only events (y)",
      "P-value (Γ=1)",
      "Γmax",
      "P-value at Γmax"
    ),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  )


# Save as Word document
save_as_docx(
  rosenbaum_table,
  path = "output/Rosenbaum_effect.docx"
)
```

### 1 Filter & match the new population

```{r filterpain}

# Filter dataset to only those who did not receive EPIDURAL
Outp <- Out %>%
  filter(EPIDURAL == "0") %>%
  mutate(
    PAIN = factor(
      PAIN,
      levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3"),
      labels = c(
        "No pain",
        "Mild pain (score 1-3)",
        "Moderate pain (score 4-6)",
        "Severe pain (score 7-10)"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# Do matching

set.seed(123)

m.outp <- matchit(
  TRT2 ~ AGS + YEARS + GENDER + BMI + PREOPRNPLN + HISTOINJ +
    SURGIND2 + PREOPVURGRADE + VURSIDE + UDR7M + VURPHASE +
    PREOPEPISODE1 + PREOPTYPEU1 + PREOPRNSCR + SURGTECH2,
  data = Outp,
  method = "nearest",
  ratio = 1,  # 1:1 matching (1 treated : 1 control)
  distance = "logit",
  caliper = 0.2   
)


mdatap <- match.data(
  m.outp,
  weights = "weightsp_psm" 
)
readr::write_csv(mdatap, "data/matched_nonepidural_data.csv") 



# Table for balance
# This gives: SMD before and after matching, and flagged imbalance (>0.1)
balmp <- cobalt::bal.tab(m.outp, un = TRUE, ESS = TRUE, m.threshold = 0.1)
balmp 

balmp_df <- as.data.frame(balmp$Balance)
smd_tablemp <- balmp_df %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = rownames(balmp_df),
    SMD_Before = round(abs(Diff.Un), 3),
    SMD_After  = round(abs(Diff.Adj), 3)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, SMD_Before, SMD_After) 

smd_tablemp %>%
  flextable() %>%
  save_as_docx(path = "output/SMD_psm_p.docx")



# Figure for balance - Love plot
# Review guidelines to decide on plotting Standardized or Absolute Mean Differences
plmp <- love.plot(
  m.outp,
  threshold = 0.1,
  abs = TRUE, # As SMD sign is meaningless for balance, show only absolute SMDs using abs = TRUE (the correct interpretation of SMD): Because SMD direction (+/-) is meaningless, only magnitude matters
  stats = "mean.diffs",       # forces SMD instead of raw differences
  var.order = "unadjusted",   # Orders variables based on imbalance before matching
  drop.distance = TRUE,      # To exclude the distance from the plot
  sample.names = c("Before matching", "After matching"),
    size = 4,
    var.names = c(
    AGS = "Age at surgery",
```

### 4 Regression

```{r regpain}

# -----------------------------------------
### Moderate-severe pain vs. Other levels
# -----------------------------------------

mdatap <- mdatap %>%
  mutate(
    PAIN_ms = factor(
      ifelse(
        PAIN %in% c(
          "Moderate pain (score 4-6)",
          "Severe pain (score 7-10)"
        ),
        1,
        0
      ),
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c(
        "No/Mild pain (score 0-3)",
        "Moderate-Severe pain (score 4-10)"
      )
    )
  )


mdatap$PAIN_ms <- ifelse(
  mdatap$PAIN_ms == "Moderate-Severe pain (score 4-10)",
  1,
  0
)

# -----------------------------------------------------
### Exploratory analysis: Severe pain vs. Other levels
# -----------------------------------------------------

mdatap <- mdatap %>%
  mutate(
    PAIN_s = factor(
      ifelse(
        PAIN == "Severe pain (score 7-10)",
        1,
        0
      ),
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c(
        "No severe pain (score 0-6)",
        "Severe pain (score 7-10)"
      )
    )
  )

# a numeric binary outcome:
mdatap$PAIN_s <- ifelse(
  mdatap$PAIN_s == "Severe pain (score 7-10)",
  1,
  0
)

#----------
# Block 1
#----------

outcomes <- c(
  "PAIN_ms",
  "PAIN_s"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
mdatap[outcomes] <- lapply(
  mdatap[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Apply GEE model after matching for all binary outcomes
gee_results_psmp <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2")
  )
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = mdatap,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weightsp_psm,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results_psmp) <- outcomes


# Combine results into one table
gee_table_psmp <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results_psmp), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results_psmp[[x]]
    tmp <- tmp %>%
      filter(grepl("^TRT2", term)) %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
    tmp
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table
gee_table_final_psmp <- gee_table_psmp %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )

gee_table_final_psmp

gee_table_final_psmp %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/pain_unadj_m.docx"
  )


#--------
# Block 2
#---------

outcomes <- c(
  "PAIN_ms",
  "PAIN_s"
)


# convert outcomes to numeric
mdatap[outcomes] <- lapply(
  mdatap[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Predictors to include in the outcome models
predictors <- c("TRT2", "STENT")


# Apply GEE model after overlap weighting for all binary outcomes
gee_results_psmp <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~",
          paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")
   )
  )  
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = mdatap,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weightsp_psm,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results_psmp) <- outcomes

# Combine results into one table
gee_table_psmp <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results_psmp), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results_psmp[[x]]
    tmp %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table
gee_table_final_psmp <- gee_table_psmp %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",

      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Predictor = term,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )

gee_table_final_psmp

)

# Function to extract treatment effects within each stent stratum
get_gee_interaction_results <- function(y) {
  
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2 * STENT")
  )
  
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = mdatap,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weightsp_psm,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  
  # Coefficients
  beta <- coef(model)
  
  # Robust covariance matrix
  V <- vcov(model)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among NO-STENT patients
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_no_stent <- beta["TRT21"]
  
  se_no_stent <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"]
  )
  
  OR_no_stent <- exp(b_no_stent)
  
  CI_no_stent <- exp(
    b_no_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_no_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LG vs Cohen among STENTED patients
  # = TRT21 + TRT21:STENT1
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_stent <- beta["TRT21"] +
    beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  # Variance of the linear combination:
  # Var(beta1 + beta3)
  
  var_stent <-
    V["TRT21", "TRT21"] +
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"] +
    2 * V["TRT21", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_stent <- sqrt(var_stent)
  
  OR_stent <- exp(b_stent)
  
  CI_stent <- exp(
    b_stent + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_stent
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Interaction test
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  b_interaction <- beta["TRT21:STENT1"]
  
  se_interaction <- sqrt(
    V["TRT21:STENT1", "TRT21:STENT1"]
  )
  
  z_interaction <- b_interaction / se_interaction
  
  p_interaction <- 2 * pnorm(
    abs(z_interaction),
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Return manuscript-ready results
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  data.frame(
    Outcome = y,
    
    `LG vs Cohen, No Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_no_stent,
        CI_no_stent[1],
        CI_no_stent[2]
      ),
    
    `LG vs Cohen, Stent` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
        OR_stent,
        CI_stent[1],
        CI_stent[2]
      ),
    
    P_interaction = p_interaction,
    
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# Run for all 2 outcomes
interaction_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(outcomes, get_gee_interaction_results)
)


interaction_results
```

### 5 Rosenbaum's sensitivity analyses 

```{r rosenbaum}

# Rosenbaum's primal sensitivity analysis

outcomes <- c(
  "PAIN_ms",
  "PAIN_s"
)

# Convert outcomes to numeric
mdatap[outcomes] <- lapply(
  mdatap[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)


# Function for Rosenbaum sensitivity analysis using rbounds
rosenbaum_binary <- function(outcome, data, match_object, 
                             gamma_seq = seq(1, 11, by = 0.1),
                            alpha = 0.05) {  
  
  # matched pairs
  treated_ids <- rownames(match_object$match.matrix)
  control_ids <- match_object$match.matrix[, 1]
  
  pairs <- data.frame(
    treated = data[treated_ids, outcome],
    control = data[control_ids, outcome]
  )
  
  # remove missing outcome pairs
  pairs <- na.omit(pairs)
  
  # discordant pairs
  # x = control has outcome, treated does not
  # y = treated has outcome, control does not
  x <- sum(pairs$control == 1 & pairs$treated == 0)
  y <- sum(pairs$treated == 1 & pairs$control == 0)
  
  # run Rosenbaum sensitivity
  if ((x + y) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      Outcome = outcome,
      Discordant_pairs = 0,
      x = x,
      y = y,
      p_Gamma1 = NA,
      gamma_max = NA,
      p_gamma_max = NA
    ))
  }
  
  # Run sensitivity over Gamma values

  gamma_results <- sapply(gamma_seq, function(g) {
    
  res <- binarysens(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      Gamma = g,
      GammaInc = 0.1  # GammaInc defines the increment used to increase Γ values when the function evaluates sensitivity.
    )

    # extract upper bound p-value corresponding to Gamma g
    res$bounds$`Upper bound`[
      res$bounds$Gamma == g
    ]
  })
  
    # p-value at Gamma = 1
    p_gamma1 <- gamma_results[gamma_seq == 1]
  
    # first Gamma where upper p-value >= alpha
    idx <- which(gamma_results < alpha)

if(length(idx) == 0){

  if(p_gamma1 >= alpha){
    
    gamma_max <- "NS at Gamma=1"
    p_gamma_max <- NA
    
  } else {
    
    gamma_max <- paste0(">=", max(gamma_seq))
    p_gamma_max <- gamma_results[length(gamma_results)]
    
  }

} else {
  
  gamma_max_value <- gamma_seq[max(idx)]
  
  # If still significant at the maximum tested Gamma
  if(gamma_max_value == max(gamma_seq)){
    
    gamma_max <- paste0(">=", max(gamma_seq))
    
  } else {
    
    gamma_max <- gamma_max_value
    
  }
  
  p_gamma_max <- gamma_results[max(idx)]
}

  # Extract p-values from rbounds object
  data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Discordant_pairs = x + y,
    x = x,
    y = y,
    p_Gamma1 = round(p_gamma1, 3),
    gamma_max = gamma_max,
    p_gamma_max = round(p_gamma_max, 3)
  )
}


# Run all outcomes
rosenbaum_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    outcomes,
    rosenbaum_binary,
    data = mdatap,
    match_object = m.outp
  )
)

rosenbaum_results


# Rename columns for publication
rosenbaum_results_pub <- rosenbaum_results %>%
  rename(
    Outcome = Outcome,
    `Discordant pairs` = Discordant_pairs,
    `Control only events (x)` = x,
    `Treated only events (y)` = y,
    `P-value (Γ=1)` = p_Gamma1,
    `Γmax` = gamma_max,
    `P-value at Γmax` = p_gamma_max
  )


# Create publication table
rosenbaum_tablep <- rosenbaum_results_pub %>%
  flextable() %>%
  
  # Add title
  add_header_lines(
    "Rosenbaum’s primal sensitivity analysis for pain in the matched cohort."
  ) %>%
  
  # Add footnote
  add_footer_lines(
    "The Gamma value Γ is a measure of sensitivity to hidden bias, representing the magnitude of differential odds of treatment assignment due to an unmeasured confounder that could alter the study conclusion. Γmax refers to the highest value of Γ for which the upper-bound p-value remained below 0.05. P-values correspond to the upper bound."
  ) %>%
  
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  
  align(
    j = c(
      "Discordant pairs",
      "Control only events (x)",
      "Treated only events (y)",
      "P-value (Γ=1)",
      "Γmax",
      "P-value at Γmax"
    ),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  )


# Save as Word document
save_as_docx(
  rosenbaum_tablep,
  path = "output/Rosenbaum_effect_pain.docx"
)
```

# SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS 3 - Not reported because there is unstable results: The conclusion is not validated on the whole population of unilateral VUR treated with Cohen and LG. Let's focus on the conclusion on population with a clinical equipoise

### 1 Do weighting: using Stabilized ATE (Sensitivity Analysis)

```{r weightingate, eval=FALSE}

# Do weighting

# The weight is a mathematical device to create the population for whom the causal effect is defined.
# The estimand (ATE, ATT, and ATO) are the different simulation to create the counterfactual population.
# Causal estimands = choice of target population

# Estimand -> Question -> Population -> Each estimand answers different clinical realities
# ATE -> What if everyone got A vs B?       -> Entire cohort    -> ATE mindset (classical epidemiology) -> ATE asks: “If every child in my hospital had Cohen vs Lich–Gregoir, what happens?”
# ATT -> What if treated got B instead?     -> Treated patients
# ATO -> What if among comparable patients? -> overlap region   -> ATO mindset (modern causal inference) -> ATO asks:“Among children where the surgeon truly had a choice, which technique performs better?”

set.seed(123) 

w.outa <- weightit(
  TRT2 ~ AGS + YEARS + GENDER + BMI + PREOPRNPLN + HISTOINJ +
    SURGIND2 + PREOPVURGRADE + VURSIDE + UDR7M + VURPHASE +
    PREOPEPISODE1 + PREOPTYPEU1 + PREOPRNSCR + SURGTECH2,
  data = Out,
  method = "ps",
  estimand = "ATE",   # ATE = Average Treatment Effect = this is standard inverse probability of treatment weighting
# "ATE" means IPTW is estimating the average treatment effect in the full population by weighting treated and control subjects using inverse probability weights.
# Other possible estimands: ATT = Average Treatment effect on the Treated = effect in treated group (most common in clinical surgery) / ATC = effect in controls (less common)
# estimand = "ATO" to perform overlap weighting.
# ATO defines: The average effect in the subpopulation where treatment assignment is most uncertain (Effect among patients where either treatment could plausibly be chosen.).
  stabilize = TRUE   # To weight based on stabilized IPTW to reduce variability in weights (reduce extreme weights)
)
Out$weights_ate <- w.outa$weights  # Add weights to the dataset
write.csv(Out, "data/weighted_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

summary(w.outa$weights)


# Table for balance
# This gives: SMD before and after weighting, and flagged imbalance (>0.1)
bala <- cobalt::bal.tab(w.outa, un = TRUE, ESS = TRUE, m.threshold = 0.1)  
# un=TRUE shows imbalance before AND after weighting, un=FALSE shows only after weighting
bala 

bal_df <- as.data.frame(bala$Balance)
smd_table <- bal_df %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = rownames(bal_df),
    SMD_Before = round(abs(Diff.Un), 3),
    SMD_After  = round(abs(Diff.Adj), 3)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, SMD_Before, SMD_After) # SMDs for each covariate individually, before and after weighting

smd_table %>%
  flextable() %>%
  save_as_docx(path = "output/SMDw_ate.docx")


# Figure for balance - Love plot
# Review guidelines to decide on plotting Standardized or Absolute Mean Differences
pla <- love.plot(
  w.outa,
  threshold = 0.1,
  abs = TRUE, # As SMD sign is meaningless for balance, show only absolute SMDs using abs = TRUE (the correct interpretation of SMD): Because SMD direction (+/-) is meaningless, only magnitude matters
  stats = "mean.diffs",       # forces SMD instead of raw differences
  var.order = "unadjusted",   # Orders variables based on imbalance before matching
  drop.distance = TRUE,      # To exclude the distance from the plot
  sample.names = c("Before ATE weighting", "After ATE weighting"),
    size = 4,
    var.names = c(
    AGS = "Age at surgery",
    YEARS = "Year of surgery",
    BMI = "Body mass index",
    GENDER = "Female gender",
    PREOPRNPLN = "Preop pyelonephritis",
    HISTOINJ = "History of injection",
    VURSIDE = "Right-sided VUR",
    UDR7M = "Ureteral dilation ≥ 7mm",
    PREOPTYPEU1 = "Preop febrile UTIs",
    PREOPRNSCR = "Preop renal scarring",
    VURPHASE_1 = "Reflux: voiding phase",
    VURPHASE_2 = "Reflux: filling phase",
    VURPHASE_3 = "Reflux: filling + voiding",
    SURGTECH2_1 = "Surgeon experience ≥100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_2 = "Surgeon experience 50-100 operations",
    SURGTECH2_3 = "Surgeon experience <50 operations",
    PREOPEPISODE1_1 = "Preop UTI episodes: 1",
    PREOPEPISODE1_2 = "Preop UTI episodes: 2",
    PREOPEPISODE1_3 = "Preop UTI episodes: ≥3",
    SURGIND2_1 = "Indication: breakthrough UTI",
    SURGIND2_2 = "Indication: high-grade reflux (III-V)",
    SURGIND2_3 = "Indication: poor compliance to medical treatment",
    SURGIND2_4 = "Indication: ineffective/poorly tolerated CAP",
    SURGIND2_5 = "Indication: other",
    PREOPVURGRADE_3 = "Preop VUR grade: III",
    PREOPVURGRADE_4 = "Preop VUR grade: IV",
    PREOPVURGRADE_5 = "Preop VUR grade: V"
  )
  )

pla <- pla +
      scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Before ATE weighting" = "#0072B2",
      "After ATE weighting" = "#D55E00"
    )
  ) +
    labs(
      x = "Absolute Standardized Differences",
      subtitle = "ATE weighted population of all children"
  ) +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(size = 0.5, color = "black"),
      panel.background = element_blank(), 
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.3, "cm"),
      panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
   )

ggsave ("figures/love_plot_w_ate.png", plot = pla, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)


# Compute mean SMD
smd_df <- bala$Balance
mean_smd_before <- mean(abs(smd_df$Diff.Un), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before weighting
mean_smd_after <- mean(abs(smd_df$Diff.Adj), na.rm = TRUE) # calculate mean SMD before weighting
mean_smd <- data.frame(
  Mean_SMD_Before = mean_smd_before,
  Mean_SMD_After = mean_smd_after
)

mean_smd


# how much effective sample size remains (overall ESS: calculated manually)?
summary(w.outa$weights)
bal.tab(w.outa)$Effective.Sample.Size
sum(w.outa$weights)^2 / sum(w.outa$weights^2)


# propensity score distribution
summary(w.outa$ps)
pl2a <-plot(summary(w.outa, type = "hist"))

```


Note: 
- PSM = “design by selection”: PSM changes the sample: Only matched pairs are analyzed -> you end up analyzing a subset of your original cohort. PSM typically estimates:ATT-like effect (effect in the matched sample, often closer to treated patients) even if not explicitly stated, PSM usually behaves like: “What is the effect in patients for whom we could find a comparable match?”

- IPTW = “design by reweighting”: IPTW changes the weights and keeps everyone. This method preserves representativeness and preferred for comparative effectiveness studies.
Disadvantages of IPTW
  - Sensitive to extreme propensity scores
  - Requires good model specification
  - Can still produce instability if overlap is poor
  
- PSM and IPTW (ATE) often agree (give same results in conclusions but not in interpretation) when:
  - There is good overlap between groups
  - Few extreme propensity scores exist
  - Treatment groups are balanced in baseline characteristics
  
  
There is no universal winner, but in modern epidemiology:
- IPTW (stabilized ATE) is preferred when:
  - You want population-level inference
  - You want policy-relevant conclusions
  - You have decent overlap
- PSM is preferred when:
  - You want a very transparent design
  - You want strict comparability
  - You accept reduced generalizability
  
  
- Think of PS distribution as answering: “Is there enough overlap in the data to support causal inference?
In my study, I have a good overlap structure:
So:
✔ Positivity assumption is reasonably satisfied
✔ Both IPTW and PSM are statistically feasible

Positivity (theoretical) is not exactly overlap (practical):
- Positivity = rule of nature: “In principle, both treatments are possible for all types of patients
- Overlap = what your dataset shows: “Do I actually have data in regions where both treatments appear?”

Estimation methods = how you use the data
  - IPTW = use all data (if overlap is sufficient)
  - PSM = restrict to overlap region
  - ATO = focus only on strong overlap region
  
Overlap is how we assess whether positivity is plausible in practice, but positivity is the underlying assumption required for causal inference and cannot be directly verified.


### 2 Descriptive analysis: AFTER ATE weighting

```{r descriptiveate, eval=FALSE}


# Create survey design object using overlap weights
design_ate <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1,   #  ids = CENTER means that patients are clustered within centers, use ids = ~1 if there is no clustering
# however, the survey package's cluster-robust variance estimation is not very reliable with very few clusters. Many statistical texts recommend caution when the number of clusters is small (often <20–30).
  data = Out,
  weights = ~weights_ate
)

# Weighted baseline characteristics
table1w_a <- design_ate %>%
  tbl_svysummary(
    by = TRT2,    # for stratification
    include = c(
      YEARS, AGS, GENDER, BMI, HISTOINJ, SURGIND2, PREOPVURGRADE, VURSIDE, UDR7M, 
         VURPHASE, PREOPTYPEU1, PREOPEPISODE1, PREOPRNPLN, PREOPRNSCR,
         SURGTECH2, CENTER 
  ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}-{p75})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1),
    missing = "ifany",  # shows missing only when present
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  # add_p(pvalue_fun = ~style_pvalue(.x, digits = 3)) %>% # add_p() is not informative after weighting
  bold_labels()

table1w_a

  ylim = c(0,1)

# ggsurvplot(pval = TRUE) calculates the p-value using a log-rank test based on the data supplied, and it does not properly account for propensity score weights.
# So the curve may be weighted, but the p-value may still come from an unweighted comparison.
# So, it is better to use a weighted Cox model then add the p-value from your weighted Cox model manually:
cox_w <- svycoxph(

)

  dpi = 300
)

# Figure: Weighted Kaplan–Meier cumulative incidence curves after ate weighting.
# Table: Weighted Cox proportional hazards model estimating the association between surgical technique and time to postoperative UTI.


# Estimated 1-year survival
s_wa <- summary(fit_w_a, times = 12, extend = TRUE)  # # The extend = TRUE is useful if there isn't an event exactly at 365 days.

# Estimated 1-year cumulative probability of UTI
uti_1yr_wa <- data.frame(
  Treatment = s_wa$strata,
  UTI_1yr = 100 * (1 - s_wa$surv),
  Lower_95CI = 100 * (1 - s_wa$upper),
  Upper_95CI = 100 * (1 - s_wa$lower)
)

uti_1yr_wa

```


### 3 Regression models

#### Block 1

```{r reg1wate, eval=FALSE}

# GEE model after ATE weighting - Accounting for center-clustering

# Block 1: technique effect on postoperative outcomes = Univariable analyses

outcomes <- c(
  "LUTD",
  "OBST",
  "URCOMPINJ",
  "SURG",
  "ILEUS",
  "GU30",
  "GU90",
  "PROC365",
  "REC011",
  "REC011_best",
  "REC011_worst"
)

# convert outcomes to numeric
Out[outcomes] <- lapply(
  Out[outcomes],
  function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
)

# Apply GEE model after ATE weighting for all binary outcomes
gee_results_ate <- lapply(outcomes, function(y) {
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste(y, "~ TRT2")
  )
  model <- geeglm(
    formula,
    data = Out,
    id = CENTER,
    weights = weights_ate,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    corstr = "exchangeable"
  )
  tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)   # estimate = OR because exponentiate = TRUE
})
names(gee_results_ate) <- outcomes


# Combine results into one table
gee_table_ate <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(gee_results_ate), function(x){
    tmp <- gee_results_ate[[x]]
    tmp <- tmp %>%
      filter(grepl("^TRT2", term)) %>%
      mutate(outcome = x)
    tmp
  })
)

# Create final manuscript table
gee_table_final_ate <- gee_table_ate %>%
  mutate(
    Effect_measure = "OR",
    Estimate = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)
    ),
    P_value = p.value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Effect_measure,
    Estimate,
    CI,
    P_value
  )


# weighted Cox model for POSTUTI

# The main issue with the clustered Cox model (using survey design object with  ids = CENTER) was the unstable variance estimation from only four clusters (a higher number of clusters is required).

cox_uti_a <- svycoxph(
  Surv(POSTUTIFUP, POSTUTI == 1) ~ TRT2 + strata(CENTER),
  design = design_ate
)

# your earlier binary GEE models are estimating a population-average effect, while this stratified Cox model estimates a center-stratified Cox effect. This difference is acceptable, but you should describe both as center-adjusted analyses rather than claiming they are exactly identical estimands.

# If you wanted HRs for each center, you would need: + factor(CENTER)

# `strata(CENTER)` allows each center to have its own baseline hazard function. It estimates the treatment effect adjusted for different baseline hazards across centers.

cox_summarya <- summary(cox_uti_a)

cox_row <- grep(
  "^TRT2",
  rownames(cox_summarya$coefficients)
)

POSTUTI_table_ate <- data.frame(
  Outcome = "POSTUTI",
  Effect_measure = "HR",
  Estimate = sprintf(
    "%.2f",
    cox_summarya$coefficients[
      cox_row,
      "exp(coef)"
    ]
  ),
  CI = paste0(
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summarya$conf.int[cox_row, "lower .95"]),
    "–",
    sprintf("%.2f",
            cox_summarya$conf.int[cox_row, "upper .95"])
  ),
  P_value = cox_summarya$coefficients[
    cox_row,
    "Pr(>|z|)"
  ]
)

# Combine final results
final_resultsa <- rbind(
  gee_table_final_ate,
  POSTUTI_table_ate
)


# Multiple correction

## Bonferroni correction
final_resultsa$p_bonferroni <- p.adjust(
  final_resultsa$P_value,
  method = "bonferroni"
)

## Holm-Bonferroni
final_resultsa$p_holm <- p.adjust(
  final_resultsa$P_value,
  method = "holm"
)

## Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
final_resultsa$p_FDR <- p.adjust(
  final_resultsa$P_value,
  method = "BH"
)


final_resultsa <- final_resultsa %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(P_value, p_bonferroni, p_holm, p_FDR),
      ~case_when(
        .x < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)
      )
    )
  )

final_resultsa

final_resultsa %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  align(
    j = c("Estimate", "CI", "P_value"),
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) %>%
  save_as_docx(
    path = "output/treatment_unadj_w_ate.docx"
  )


# Evaluate whether CENTER distribution is balanced after weighting, despite that CENTER was not included in weighting

# bal.tab(
#   w.outa,
#   data = Out,
#   addl = ~ CENTER
# )

# Results showed that all CENTER SMD < 0.05 → excellent balance
# Therefore, after ATO weighting, CENTER is well balanced between treatment groups.
# This is an important finding because your original data showed strong center-treatment imbalance.
# Why did CENTER become balanced although it was not in the propensity score model?
# This is possible because CENTER was correlated with the covariates you included in the propensity model.
```
